This vignette discusses how to add a new **XH** module to [`ramp.library`](https://github.com/dd-harp/ramp.library). As background, 
we strongly recommend reading the **`ramp.xds`** vignette about the [**XH** Interface.](https://dd-harp.github.io/ramp.xds/articles/XH-interface.html)

Each **XH** module implements a unique model family describing human/host infection dynamics and immunity that can be used by  [`ramp.xds`](https://github.com/dd-harp/ramp.xds). Before writing a new module, please check and see if the model family is already part of the SimBA library. 

If you need help, please contact [Professor David L Smith](mailto:smitdave@gmail.com)

*** 

We have written this vignette to produce a new template file using `knitr::purl.` The template can be modified to build a new **XH** module. 

Do this:

1. Download the markdown file that created this document ["X-How_To_Add_Model.Rmd."](https://github.com/dd-harp/ramp.library/blob/main/vignettes/X-How_To_Add_Model.Rmd)

2. Set your working directory to the location of the downloaded copy of "X-How_To_Add_Model.Rmd"

3. Execute these commands:

```{r, purl=F, eval=F}
library(knitr)
knitr::purl("X-How_To_Add_Model.Rmd", 
            output = "XHmodule-newXHname.R", 
            documentation = 0, 
            quiet=TRUE)
```

4. You should see a new file called `XHmodule-newXHname.R` in the working directory. You can now move and rename it. 

5. Open the file and do a global search for `newXHname` and replace it with a short string that will define the model as its `XHname`.

6. Edit the functions following the directions below.  

## Style Guide 

We recommend that new models conform to a set of style guidelines:

+ Retrieve state variables by name using the indices attached to `XH_obj`.
+ All documentation is written in `roxygen2`

+ Functions should use `with(*,{...})` to make the code easier to read. 

+ A vignette should accompany each model, including citations to the relevant publications, and proposed tests of the code.  

+ The functions should be easy to relate to the equations defining a model, following notation defined in an accompanying vignette.

## Dynamics 


### dXHdt 

The sections that need to be modified are marked `# Change this`

+ Replace `X1` with the name of your first state variable, and replace `F_1` with the formula that computes its derivative. Do the same with `X2` and add lines for each state variable.

+ The method reads the stored FoI from `xds_obj$terms$FoI[[i]]`. Use the shared `Births(t, y, xds_obj, i)` and `Deaths` functions for demographic terms, as shown below. Return derivatives in the same order as the indexed state variables.

```{r}
#' @title Compute the derivatives for parasite infection dynamics in human population strata 
#' @description Implements [dXHdt] for the newXHname model
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::dXHdt
#' @return a [numeric] vector
#' @export
dXHdt.newXHname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, i) {

  # do not change this
  foi <- xds_obj$terms$FoI[[i]]

  # do not change this
  # attach the variables by name 
  with(get_XH_vars(y, xds_obj, i),{
    # do not change this
    # attach the parameters by name 
    with(xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]], {
      # Do not change this 
      dH <- Births(t, y, xds_obj, i) - Deaths(t, H, xds_obj, i)
      # Change this
      dX1 <- F_1(foi, X1, X2) - Deaths(t, X1, xds_obj, i)
      dX2 <- F_2(foi, X1, X2) - Deaths(t, X2, xds_obj, i)
      
      # Change this 
      derivs <- c(dH, dX1, dX2)
      
      # return the derivatives 
      return(derivs)
    })
  })
}
```

### Update_XHt (discrete-time modules)

This is the discrete-time alternative to `dXHdt`; the continuous-time `SIS` module does not define `Update_XHt.SIS`.

```{r}
#' @title Compute the derivatives for parasite infection dynamics in human population strata 
#' @description Implements [Update_XHt] for the newXHname model
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::Update_XHt
#' @return a [numeric] vector
#' @export
Update_XHt.newXHname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, i) {
  ar <- xds_obj$terms$AR[[i]]

  # do not change this
  # attach the variables by name 
  with(get_XH_vars(y, xds_obj, i),{
    # do not change this
    # attach the parameters by name 
    with(xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]], {
      # For a static-population example; add demographic updates if needed.
      Ht <- H
      # Change this. Use ar for infection events in a discrete-time model.
      X1t <- X1 + F_1(ar, X1, X2)
      X2t <- X2 + F_2(ar, X1, X2)
      
      # Change this 
      states <- c(Ht, X1t, X2t)
      
      # return the updated state variables
      return(states)
    })
  })
}
```


## XH Model Object 

### make_XH_obj

+ In the following, replace `p1` with the first parameter, `p2` with the second, and so on.

+ Shared demographic and mass-treatment features are initialized by `setup_XH_obj` using the `ramp.xds` setup functions; do not create a separate demographic matrix or replace these ports in `make_XH_obj`.
+ If the module supports mass drug administration or mass screen and treat, include the corresponding treatment terms in its state updates and record that capability in `get_skillset_XH.newXHname`.

```{r}
#' @title Make a `newXHname` **XH** model object
#' @param nStrata is the number of population strata
#' @param options a [list] that could override defaults
#' @param p1 the first parameter 
#' @param p2 the second parameter 
#' @param p3 the third parameter 
#' @return a [list]
#' @export
make_XH_obj_newXHname = function(nStrata, options=list(),
                         p1=1, p2=2, p3=3){
  with(options,{
    XH_obj = list()
    class(XH_obj) <- c("newXHname")

    # Change this
    XH_obj$p1 = checkIt(p1, nStrata)
    XH_obj$p2 = checkIt(p2, nStrata)
    XH_obj$p3 = checkIt(p3, nStrata)

    return(XH_obj)
  })}
```


### setup_XH_obj  

This method also initializes the shared XH interface features. Follow the setup sequence used by existing modules.

```{r}
#' @title Setup XH_obj.newXHname
#' @description Implements [setup_XH_obj] for the newXHname model
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::setup_XH_obj
#' @return an **`xds`** object
#' @export
setup_XH_obj.newXHname = function(XHname, residence, xds_obj, options=list(), i=1){
  xds_obj$XHname = "newXHname"
  xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]] = make_XH_obj_newXHname(xds_obj$nStrata[i], options)
  xds_obj <- setup_XH_inits(xds_obj, options=options, i=i)
  xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$skill_set <- get_skillset_XH(xds_obj, i)
  xds_obj <- setup_blood_search_weights("setup", xds_obj, i=i)
  xds_obj <- setup_timespent("setup", xds_obj, list(residence=residence), i)
  xds_obj <- setup_mass_treatment(xds_obj, i=i)
  xds_obj <- setup_demog_obj(xds_obj, i)
  xds_obj <- setup_time_away("setup", xds_obj, i=i)
  xds_obj <- setup_travel_eir("no_travel", xds_obj, i=i)
  return(xds_obj)
}
```

## Parameters 

Implement methods to inspect and change the module's parameters. The `options` argument is a named list; parameters not supplied in `options` retain their existing values when changed.

```{r}
#' @title Get parameters for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_XH_pars
#' @return a [list]
#' @export
get_XH_pars.newXHname <- function(xds_obj, i=1) {
  with(xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]], list(p1=p1, p2=p2, p3=p3))
}

#' @title Change parameters for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::change_XH_pars
#' @return an **`xds`** object
#' @export
change_XH_pars.newXHname <- function(xds_obj, options=list(), i=1) {
  with(xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]], with(options, {
    if (!is.null(p1)) xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$p1 <- p1
    if (!is.null(p2)) xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$p2 <- p2
    if (!is.null(p3)) xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$p3 <- p3
    xds_obj
  }))
}
```

## Variables 

### setup_XH_ix  

In the following, each variable in your model gets its own pair of lines. Replace `X1` in `X1_ix` with the first variable name, `X2` in `X2_ix` with the second, and add lines for each variable by copying and pasting and editing the pair of lines. Be sure the replacement gets applied to all four instances.  


```{r}
#' @title Add indices for human population variables
#' @description Implements [setup_XH_ix] for the newXHname model.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::setup_XH_ix
#' @return none
#' @importFrom utils tail
#' @export
setup_XH_ix.newXHname <- function(xds_obj, i) {with(xds_obj,{

  H_ix <- seq(from = max_ix+1, length.out=xds_obj$nStrata[i])
  max_ix <- tail(H_ix, 1)
  
  X1_ix <- seq(from = max_ix+1, length.out=xds_obj$nStrata[i])
  max_ix <- tail(X1_ix, 1)

  X2_ix <- seq(from = max_ix+1, length.out=xds_obj$nStrata[i])
  max_ix <- tail(X2_ix, 1)
  
  xds_obj$max_ix = max_ix
  xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$ix = list(H_ix=H_ix, X1_ix=X1_ix, X2_ix=X2_ix)
  return(xds_obj)
})}
```

### get_XH_vars   

In the following, each variable in your model gets its own pair of lines. 

+ Leave `H` as-is 

+ Replace `X1` in `X1` and `X1_ix` with the first variable name. 

+ Replace `X2` in `X2` and `X2_ix` with the second variable name. 

+ Copy the form for every other variable 

+ The variable `X0` is the class that gets newborns. If you use it or if you want to have it available, compute it and add it to the returned list. 

```{r}
#' @title Return the variables as a list
#' @description This method dispatches on the type of `xds_obj$XH_obj`
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_XH_vars
#' @return a [list]
#' @export
get_XH_vars.newXHname <- function(y, xds_obj, i) {
  with(xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$ix,{
      H = y[H_ix]
      X1 = y[X1_ix]
      X2 = y[X2_ix]
      X0 = H-X1-X2 
      return(list(H=H, X1=X1, X2=X2, X0=X0))})
}
``` 

### parse_XH_orbits  

In the following, each variable in your model gets its own pair of lines. 

+ Leave `H` as-is 

+ Replace `X1` in `X1` and `X1_ix` with the first variable name. 

+ Replace `X2` in `X2` and `X2_ix` with the second variable name. 

+ Copy the form for every other variable 

+ The variable `X0` is the class that gets newborns. If you use it or if you want to have it available, compute it and add it to the returned list.

```{r}
#' @title parse the output of deSolve and return variables for the newXHname model
#' @description Implements [parse_XH_orbits] for the newXHname model
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::parse_XH_orbits
#' @return a named list  
#' @export
parse_XH_orbits.newXHname <- function(outputs, xds_obj, i) {
  with(xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$ix,{
    H <- outputs[,H_ix]
    X1 <- outputs[,X1_ix]
    X2 <- outputs[,X2_ix]
    X0 <- H-X1-X2
    vars <- list(H=H, X1=X1, X2=X2, X0=X0)
    return(vars)
})}
```
 

## Initial Values 

### setup_XH_inits

If you did the global search and replace, you won't need to change this function. 

```{r}
#' @title Setup initial values for *newXHname*
#' 
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::setup_XH_inits
#' 
#' @return a **`ramp.xds`** object 
#' 
#' @export
setup_XH_inits.newXHname = function(xds_obj, options=list(), i=1){
  xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$inits = make_XH_inits_newXHname(xds_obj$nStrata[i], options=options)
  return(xds_obj)
}
```

### make_XH_inits

```{r}
#' @title Make initial values for the XHname human model, with defaults
#' @param nStrata the number of strata in the model
#' @param options a [list] to override defaults
#' @param X1 the initial value for X1 
#' @param X2 the initial value for X2
#' @return a [list]
#' @export
make_XH_inits_newXHname = function(nStrata, options = list(), H=1000, X1=1, X2=1){with(options,{
  H = unname(as.vector(checkIt(H, nStrata)))
  X1 = unname(as.vector(checkIt(X1, nStrata)))
  X2 = unname(as.vector(checkIt(X2, nStrata)))
  return(list(H=H, X1=X1, X2=X2))
})}
```

### change_XH_inits 

```{r}
#' @title Change initial values for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' 
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::change_XH_inits 
#' 
#' @return an **`xds`** object
#' @export
change_XH_inits.newXHname <- function(xds_obj, options=list(), i=1) {
  with(get_XH_inits(xds_obj, i), with(options,{
    xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$inits$H = H
    xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$inits$X1 = X1
    xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$inits$X2 = X2
    return(xds_obj)
  }))}
```


## Dynamical Terms   


### F_I

Replace `p1*X1` with the model's formula for effective infectious host density: state density weighted by the probability of transmitting.

```{r}
#' @title Size of effective infectious human population
#' @description Implements [F_I] for the newXHname model.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_I
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nStrata`
#' @export
F_I.newXHname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, i) {
  with(get_XH_vars(y, xds_obj, i), {
    with(xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]], {
      infectious_density <- p1*X1
      return(infectious_density)
    })
  })
}
```

### F_H  

If you did the global search and replace, and have not changed the name of `H`, this method may not need to be changed.

```{r}
#' @title Size of human population
#' @description Implements [F_H] for the newXHname model.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_H
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nStrata`
#' @export
F_H.newXHname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, i){
  return(get_XH_vars(y, xds_obj, i)$H)
}
```

### F_infectivity  

If you use `p1` for the probability of getting infected per infectious bite, don't change anything.

```{r}
#' @title Infection blocking pre-erythrocytic immunity
#' @description Implements [F_infectivity] for the newXHname model.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_infectivity
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nStrata`
#' @export
F_infectivity.newXHname <- function(y, xds_obj, i) {
  with(xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]],{ 
    ########################
    # retrieve or compute it 
    ########################
    b = xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$p1
    ########################
    # return it 
    ########################
    return(b)
  })
}
```


## Other Outputs  

To make `ramp.xds` easy to use, we provide some functions that parse the outputs and compute some standard metrics. 

### F_prevalence

Replace `X1/H` with the formula  to compute prevalence. 

```{r}
#' @title Compute the true prevalence of infection / parasite rate
#' @description Implements [F_prevalence] for the newXHname model.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_prevalence
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nStrata`
#' @export
F_prevalence.newXHname <- function(vars, XH_obj) {
  with(vars, X1/H)
}
```

### F_ni

Replace `p1*X1/H` with the model's formula for net infectiousness.

```{r}
#' @title Compute net infectiousness for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @description Implements [F_ni] for the newXHname model.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_ni
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nStrata`
#' @export
F_ni.newXHname <- function(vars, XH_obj) {
  with(vars, with(XH_obj, p1*X1/H))
}
```

### get_HTC

```{r}
#' @title Compute human transmitting capacity for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @description Implements [get_HTC] for the newXHname model.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_HTC
#' @return a [numeric] vector
#' @export
get_HTC.newXHname <- function(xds_obj, i) {
  stop("Replace this with the model's human transmitting capacity formula")
}
```

## Internal Consistency

Every model provides a skill-set method and a check method. The former returns supported capabilities as a list; setup stores that list on the module object. The latter can check or update the model before solving.

```{r}
#' @title Get the skill set for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_skillset_XH
#' @return the **XH** module skill set, as a list
#' @export
get_skillset_XH.newXHname <- function(xds_obj, i) {
  list(
    delay=FALSE,
    demography=TRUE,
    prevalence=TRUE,
    malaria=TRUE,
    diagnostics="linear"
  )
}

#' @title Check `newXHname` before solving
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::check_XH
#' @return an **`xds`** object
#' @export
check_XH.newXHname <- function(xds_obj, i) {
  xds_obj
}
```

## Optional Functions

### Diagnostic prevalence

The `SIS` module implements these three methods. Other modules can implement the methods relevant to their diagnostic outputs; replace `X1/H` and the diagnostic parameter names below with the appropriate formulas and parameters for the model.

```{r}
#' @title Compute prevalence by light microscopy
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_prevalence
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nStrata`
#' @export
F_pfpr_by_lm.newXHname <- function(vars, XH_obj) {
  with(vars, with(XH_obj, q_lm*X1/H))
}

#' @title Compute prevalence by RDT
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_prevalence
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nStrata`
#' @export
F_pfpr_by_rdt.newXHname <- function(vars, XH_obj) {
  with(vars, with(XH_obj, q_rdt*X1/H))
}

#' @title Compute prevalence by PCR
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_prevalence
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nStrata`
#' @export
F_pfpr_by_pcr.newXHname <- function(vars, XH_obj) {
  with(vars, with(XH_obj, q_pcr*X1/H))
}
```

### Steady states

`steady_state_X` is optional and is implemented by `SIS`. If useful for the model, implement the method for the **X** component as a function of FoI and host density.

```{r}
#' @title Compute steady states for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::steady_state_X
#' @return a named list of steady-state variables
#' @export
steady_state_X.newXHname <- function(foi, H, xds_obj, i=1) {
  stop("Replace this with the model's steady-state calculation")
}
```

### Plotting

### Module-specific line plotting function

#### add_lines_X_newXHname

```{r}
#' Add lines for the `newXHname` state variables
#'
#' @param time simulation time points
#' @param XH a list with the outputs of parse_XH_orbits.newXHname
#' @param nStrata the number of population strata
#' @param clrs a vector of colors
#' @param llty an integer (or integers) to set the `lty` for plotting
#'
#' @export
add_lines_X_newXHname = function(time, XH, nStrata, clrs=c("darkblue","darkred"), llty=1){
  with(XH,{
    if(nStrata==1) {
      lines(time, X1, col=clrs[1], lty = llty[1])
      lines(time, X2, col=clrs[2], lty = llty[1])
    }
    if(nStrata>1){
      if (length(clrs)==2) clrs=matrix(clrs, 2, nStrata)
      if (length(llty)==1) llty=rep(llty, nStrata)

      for(i in 1:nStrata){
        lines(time, X1[,i], col=clrs[1,i], lty = llty[i])
        lines(time, X2[,i], col=clrs[2,i], lty = llty[i])
      }
    }
  })}
```

### xds_plot_X

The module-specific line plotting function is called by its `xds_plot_X` method.

#### Generic

```{r, eval=F, purl=F}
#' Basic plotting for epidemiological models
#'
#' @param xds_obj a list that defines an `ramp.xds` model (*e.g.*,  generated by `xde_setup()`)
#' @param i the host species index
#' @param clrs a vector of colors
#' @param llty an integer (or integers) to set the `lty` for plotting
#' @param add plot axes only if FALSE
#'
#' @export
xds_plot_X = function(xds_obj, i=1, clrs="black", llty=1, add=FALSE){
  UseMethod("xds_plot_X", xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]])
}
```

#### xds_plot_X.newXHname

```{r}
#' Plot the density of infected individuals for the newXHname model
#'
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::xds_plot_X
#' @export
xds_plot_X.newXHname = function(xds_obj, i=1, clrs=c("darkblue","darkred"), llty=1, add=FALSE){
  XH <- xds_obj$outputs$orbits$XH[[i]]
  time <- xds_obj$outputs$time
  if (add==FALSE)
    plot(time, 0*time, type="n", ylim=c(0, max(XH$H)),
         ylab="State density", xlab="Time")
  add_lines_X_newXHname(time, XH, xds_obj$nStrata[i], clrs, llty)
}
```


## Reusable Code 

**`ramp.xds`** has a modular design. The modular design makes it possible to break down published models to serve as dynamical components in new models for malaria, a kind of plug-and-play functionality for two kinds of systems: 

+ systems of ordinary and delay differential equations models for malaria and other mosquito-transmitted pathogens. 

+ stochastic and deterministic discrete time systems for malaria and other mosquito-transmitted pathogens. 

This package -- `ramp.library` -- is a collection of models to implement a large number of dynamical model families and other algorithms taken from the literature describing malaria and other mosquito-transmitted pathogens (see Reiner, *et al.* 2013)^[Reiner RC Jr, Perkins TA, Barker CM, Niu T, Chaves LF, Ellis AM, et al. A systematic review of mathematical models of mosquito-borne pathogen transmission: 1970-2010. J R Soc Interface. 2013;10: 20120921.]. Those models have been implemented here as code that has undergone rigorous testing and that can be used to build models for simulation-based analytics.  

The mathematics supporting this framework were explained in [Spatial Dynamics of Malaria Transmission](https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010684){target="_blank"}
^[Wu SL, Henry JM, Citron DT, Mbabazi Ssebuliba D, Nakakawa Nsumba J, Sánchez C. HM, et al. (2023) Spatial dynamics of malaria transmission. PLoS Comput Biol 19(6): e1010684. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010684] 

This vignette was written to help add new modules to `ramp.library`.
